pairs.difference: A: pure red cart body and awning, orange-gold frame and a blue backing give several real hue roles, all within the real ranges. B: the grey console is close to colorless (subject chroma 0.044, under the real floor of 0.071). In the lens the red and yellow buttons collapse into one orange, so the card reads as orange plus grey (hue families 2.31, warm share 0.94, both outside the real range). A's cream and pure red are also a little pushed, so this is not a strong call.
pairs.fix: Give the console a colored painted metal body, such as deep teal or navy, with grey only on the trim. Keep the red and yellow buttons as clearly separate hues. Make the backdrop less orange and let the floor stay a cool grey.

pairs.difference: A: the blue shoes carry green collars, teal laces, and magenta and orange accents on the laces and sole, on an orange and yellow backdrop. That is 5.49 hue families, above the real top of 4.78, with no single accent. B: a restrained white shell, one amber visor and one red stripe on pink, all within range for subject color and hue count. Both backgrounds sit just under the real floor, so that does not separate them.
pairs.fix: Make the shoes blue and white with one accent color only. Remove the neon green, magenta and orange from the laces and sole, and use plain white or pale grey laces.

pairs.difference: B: the grey saucer has almost no local color (subject chroma 0.073). Its shadow side turns dull brown-grey, keeping only 0.34 of the chroma against a real floor of 0.74, and the yellow backdrop pushes warm share to 0.89. A: an orange player on violet has its own problems. The body is one flat pure orange mass in the lens, and the background is too loud (0.238). B misses on three fields and A on two, so the call is weak, and A could also be generated.
pairs.fix: Paint the saucer hull a colored metal, such as blue-teal or deep red, instead of plain grey. Tint its underside shadow with rich blue-violet instead of muddy grey-brown.

pairs.difference: A: a yellow hull shading into orange-brown on a deep green backdrop; the background chroma of 0.095 is slightly under the real floor. B: red fins and a silver body that takes a cyan cast in the lens, on bright cyan, all in range but with a low hue count of 2.26. Both show strong hero-against-background hue roles like the real cards, and neither has a clear color fault.

A: the regolith, dome frame, sky and shadows are all tinted the same lilac, and the yellow door is the only separate accent. Warm share is 0.078 and hue families 2.96, just under the real range, so the base has little local color of its own. B: pineapple, grapes, wood thatch, green stools and teal water each keep believable local color, like the real scene cards. Its hue count of 7.05 is a little high, but the variety comes from real objects.
pairs.fix: Make the moon ground a true neutral grey with warm and cool variation, not lilac. Give the base white panels and metal parts their own colors, and keep purple only in the sky.

pairs.difference: A: flat pure violet stripes are about twice as loud as the planet (background 0.272 against subject 0.137; real top 0.217). The planet and ring are only orange and yellow, with 1.9 hue families, under the real floor. There is no neutral to rest the eye. B: coral sandals with yellow straps on teal, all within the real ranges, with a clear hero-against-background hue role.
pairs.fix: Lower the violet background to a softer, slightly greyed purple so it is quieter than the planet. Give the planet some cooler banding, such as dusty blue-grey or muted brown, instead of only orange and yellow.

pairs.difference: A is the same rose arch as in the real reference sheet: pink backdrop, green leaves, brown wood and grey iron, each with its own local color. B: the column is warm cream throughout, its shadows slide to brown-mauve, and the plinth and sign go orange and yellow, so warm share is 0.96, above the real top of 0.87. In the lens the gold sign merges into the column's tan. This matches the cream-white warm drift of the generated monitors in the lessons.
pairs.fix: Make the column a cooler off-white marble with blue-grey shadows, not cream with brown shadows. Keep the gold sign a clearly separate yellow.

pairs.difference: B: the rock is low-chroma brown (subject 0.081, just under the real floor), and its dark side drops to dull mauve-brown, keeping 0.53 of the chroma (real floor 0.74). In the lens the flames merge into the same brown mass as the rock. A: the scarf is a very pure red (0.217, above the real top of 0.189), but its shadows stay rich crimson and the gold badge is a clean accent. A is also pushed, so this is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Keep the meteor rock's shadows colored, shifting to deep violet-blue rather than dull grey-brown. Keep the flames a clearly separate orange-yellow from the rock.

pairs.difference: A: the dish and pylon are nearly colorless cream and grey (subject chroma 0.030, far under the real floor of 0.051). The hero is much quieter than the blue sky and orange sand, and the small red beacon is the only color on it. B: the orange sand castle with a green bucket and blue spade has clear hue roles and all fields in range.
pairs.fix: Paint the dish and tower a colored finish, such as a blue or red-and-white painted pattern, so the hero holds more color than the sand and sky.

pairs.difference: A: the cream stone fountain with pale cyan water on yellow stripes is warm (0.859, right at the real top) and quiet (0.071, right at the floor). B: green body with a white stripe on orange. Its low shadow chroma of 0.34 comes mostly from the black rubber bumper and dark seat, which are believable local colors. Each sits at the edge of the range on one field, and neither has a clear color fault.

B: the cream tube and moon ground share the same mauve-grey mass in the lens, and the teal background is dulled (0.091, under the real floor of 0.099), with 2.9 hue families, just under range. The cream tube is the warm off-white drift seen in the lessons. A: green barrels, black rubber and blue lenses on orange planks read as clear separate hues. Its low shadow chroma of 0.425 is mostly the black rubber, which is local color.
pairs.fix: Paint the telescope tube a stronger color, such as deep blue or green, instead of cream. Make the ground a clearly neutral grey and the teal background a little richer.

pairs.difference: B: the rover is almost colorless white and grey (subject chroma 0.019 against a real floor of 0.071) on a lime backdrop. Warm share is 0.02, hue families 1.69 and shadow chroma 0.37, all outside the real range. In the lens only lime and grey remain, and the single orange antenna tip is lost. A: the yellow taxi on blue with neutral road is a clear hero-against-background hue role, like the real cards, with only shadow chroma marginally low.
pairs.fix: Paint the rover body a bold color, such as red-orange or yellow, with white panels only as trim. Add warm color to the ground and let the shadow under the rover take a blue-violet tint, not plain grey.

pattern: The main giveaway is a colorless hero on a saturated flat backdrop: grey or cream objects (console, UFO, dish, rover) fall under the real subject-chroma floor, so the background carries all the color while real heroes keep their own local color. The second giveaway runs the other way and is the one the lessons show: colored objects get pushed, with pure single-hue masses, backgrounds louder than the hero, whites drifting to warm cream, shadows that drift warm or go muddy brown-grey, and neutrals tinted one hue across the card. Scattered neon accents also appear, where real cards keep one accent. These signals are weak on many pairs, and only p07 and p12 are strong calls. p07 rests partly on A matching the real reference sheet.
